context: Temperate agricultural soils; geometric mean ~0.005; highly variable with soil clay content
physics_mechanism: Cs+ mimics K+ in plant potassium uptake channels; strongly fixed by illite/vermiculite clay minerals in agricultural soils → low bioavailability; addition of K fertilizer competes and reduces uptake 33-50%
notes: Transfer factors decreased >50-fold 1986-1996 due to Cs-137 fixation in clay minerals; early 1986 values much higher before soil fixation occurred
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; Nisbet and Woodman 2000 Health Physics PMID:10688450

context: Temperate conditions; lettuce spinach cabbage; higher transfer than cereals due to shallow root feeding in organic layer
physics_mechanism: Higher in leafy vegetables because root-feeding zone overlaps with surface organic horizon where Cs-137 is less fixed; also foliar absorption pathway in first days
notes: Leafy vegetables had highest Cs-137 contamination in May 1986 via direct foliar deposition; post-1986 soil ingestion pathway dominates
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; Chernobyl Forum environment group 2005

context: Root vegetables (potato carrot beet); intermediate between cereals and leafy; skin contamination important
physics_mechanism: Root penetration into clay-rich subsoil where Cs more fixed; direct surface contamination of skin requires washing; inner flesh lower activity than skin
notes: Potato in Belarus/Ukraine: Cs-137 in skin 3-5x higher than inner flesh; peeling reduces intake by ~60%
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; Chernobyl Forum environment 2005

context: Grass for hay and silage; temperate conditions; geometric mean ~0.028; higher in organic soils
physics_mechanism: Grass roots in shallow zone; organic soils have lower clay fixation → higher Fv; liming increases pH and reduces Cs uptake
notes: Grass was primary exposure pathway for milk/meat contamination in 1986; 14000 Swedish lakes banned for fishing; grass-fed livestock dominated food contamination
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; food_agricultural_contamination_REAL.csv

context: Extremely high variability by species; Cantharellus Boletus Tricholoma most elevated; geometric mean ~1.0
physics_mechanism: Mycorrhizal fungi have direct hypha-to-soil contact throughout organic horizon; no clay fixation mechanism in fungal uptake; Cs-137 in organic layer (where fungi feed) less fixed than in mineral soil
notes: Primary reason for persistent mushroom contamination 40 years later; some species (Cortinarius sp.) Fv >10; safe species (chanterelle) Fv ~0.5; Bavaria Germany still restrictions on certain mushroom species 2024
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; GRS gGmbH Cs-137 mushrooms; Rosen et al. 1999

context: Wild berries (bilberry Vaccinium myrtillus; cranberry; lingonberry); high Fv in Chernobyl-affected forests
physics_mechanism: Ericaceous plants like bilberry have shallow surface roots in organic horizon; similar mechanism to mushrooms; high organic matter feeding zone
notes: Bilberry still 500-5000 Bq/kg in some CEZ forest areas 2020; major dietary source for rural Ukrainians/Belarusians; 2020 wildfires resuspended contaminated soil then deposited on berries
source: Chernobyl Forum 2005; CEZ monitoring data

context: Fm = fraction of daily Cs-137 intake by cow transferred per liter milk; at steady state
physics_mechanism: Cs mimics K → absorbed from GI tract; distributes to muscle and milk; Fm is metabolic transfer coefficient; higher in early lactation
notes: Fm used in food chain models: milk_conc (Bq/L) = Fm × daily_intake (Bq/day); 1986 Soviet milk ban too late by 2-3 weeks
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; PMC transport model; food_agricultural_contamination_REAL.csv

context: Fm for beef muscle (skeletal muscle); higher than milk; wild boar values much higher (forest Cs-137 diet)
physics_mechanism: Cs distributed throughout muscle tissue proportional to K distribution; t1/2 biological = 70-140 days in humans; shorter in smaller mammals
notes: Wild boar mean 46000 Bq/kg (CEZ 2020) = 77x EU limit 600 Bq/kg; dietary accumulation via mushrooms/berries dominates; same mechanism as cez_wildlife_contamination_REAL.csv
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; cez_wildlife_contamination_REAL.csv

context: Temperate conditions; Sr-90 transfer generally 5-10x higher than Cs-137 per unit soil activity
physics_mechanism: Sr2+ mimics Ca2+ in calcium uptake; not fixed by clay minerals like Cs; remains in exchangeable soil fraction → more mobile; liming increases Ca competition and reduces Sr-90 uptake by 50-70%
notes: Sr-90 higher mobility in soils = greater groundwater contamination risk; bone-seeker after ingestion; K fertilizer does NOT reduce Sr-90 uptake (only affects Cs-137)
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; UNSCEAR 2008; ScienceDirect 2020 Ukrainian grain Sr-90

context: Much higher than Cs-137; reflects Ca-mimicking and absence of clay fixation
physics_mechanism: Highest Fv of common crops for Sr-90; calciferous plants accumulate more; liming soil reduces by replacing exchangeable Sr with Ca
notes: UNSCEAR 2008 stresses Sr-90 bone dose in children as key dose pathway; bone-to-soft tissue dose ratio ~30 for Sr-90 vs ~1 for Cs-137
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; UNSCEAR 2008 Annex D

context: Potato carrot beet; intermediate values; soil particle adhesion also contributes
physics_mechanism: Sr-90 in root zone follows Ca movement; more mobile than Cs-137; higher in contaminated groundwater-irrigated areas
notes: Ukrainian regions still monitoring Sr-90 in food crops; near Chernobyl some soils still above 70 kBq/m2 Sr-90 threshold
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; Ukrainian ScienceDirect 2020

context: Grass and hay; higher than Cs-137 because Ca-mimicking in grass nutrition
physics_mechanism: Grass Ca content determines Sr-90 uptake; dairy cattle absorbing Sr-90 from grass transfer to milk; Sr-90 bone dose pathway for children
notes: Post-Chernobyl monitoring: Sr-90 in milk of Belarus/Ukraine farms continued to be elevated until mid-1990s
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; Chernobyl Forum 2005

context: Lower Fm than Cs-137 but higher soil Fv → comparable milk concentrations; bone accumulation means less secreted to milk
physics_mechanism: Sr absorbed from GI tract; partitioned between bone and soft tissue/milk; biological half-life in bone ~50 years; steady-state secretion to milk = small fraction of body burden
notes: Key Sr-90 dose pathway: infant bone doses from Sr-90 in contaminated milk in 1986-1990 Belarus/Ukraine; pre-school children most vulnerable
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; UNSCEAR 2008 Table B5

context: Depends on biomass and growth stage at time of deposition; geometric mean ~0.3-0.5 growing season
physics_mechanism: Foliar interception: I-131 in aerosol and gas deposits on leaf surfaces; gaseous I2 and organic iodine have higher deposition velocities than aerosol; rain dramatically increases deposition (wet vs dry)
notes: Critical window: May 1986 in USSR; cows grazing on contaminated pasture; direct deposition → grass → milk → human thyroid; weathering half-life ~10 days from pasture
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; J Environ Radioact I-131 Belarus doi:10.1016/j.jenvrad.2022.106975

context: Fm = 4.0 × 10⁻³ d/L median from post-Chernobyl Belarus measurements; range 6.7 × 10⁻³ geometric mean ± 8.7 × 10⁻³
physics_mechanism: I-131 rapidly absorbed from gut → blood → thyroid (organified) and milk; biological t1/2 in cow milk ~10 days = longer than physical t1/2 (8.02 days) so both decay simultaneously
notes: USSR delay in milk ban = primary preventable thyroid dose; Poland distributed KI to 18M → much lower thyroid doses despite similar deposition; decontamination_countermeasures_REAL.csv
source: PMC I-131 Belarus Fm doi:10.1016/j.jenvrad.2022.106975; IAEA TRS 472 2010

context: Sheep milk Fm = ~0.29 ± 0.017 d/L; ~50-100x higher than cow milk
physics_mechanism: Sheep produce much less milk (L/day) than cows; same daily intake → higher concentration per liter; sheep milk consumption in some affected European regions led to elevated thyroid doses
notes: Goat milk also 10-50x higher Fm than cow milk; important for communities using small ruminants (common in parts of Ukraine/Russia countryside)
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010

context: Main dose pathway: fresh contaminated cow milk consumed by children in 1986; thyroid dose = intake × Fm × cow feeding × thyroid uptake fraction
physics_mechanism: Children (0-6 yr) received highest thyroid doses because: 1) drink more milk per kg body weight; 2) smaller thyroid → higher dose per Bq; 3) higher thyroid 131-I uptake fraction in growing children; 4) higher RBE concern not formally quantified
notes: UNSCEAR 2008 p.59: 26% of Belarus pre-school evacuees received >5 Gy thyroid; KI could have reduced by ~90% if given within 2h; decontamination_countermeasures_REAL.csv
source: UNSCEAR 2008 Annex D Table B5; thyroid_cancer_timeseries_REAL.csv

context: Post-Chernobyl Ukrainian/Belarusian measurements; grain portion only (lower than bran)
physics_mechanism: Pu in soil exists predominantly as insoluble hydroxide/oxide or bound in fuel particle matrix; extremely low solubility = low root uptake; Pu4+ forms stable soil colloids; minimal food chain transfer
notes: Pu dose pathway: inhalation of resuspended soil particles >> ingestion; dietary Pu from Chernobyl negligible compared to weapons test fallout; UNSCEAR: dietary Pu dose below detection
source: Soil-to-plant Pu Belarus Chernobyl PMID:15196842; IAEA TRS 472 2010

context: Root vegetables; range reflects soil type variability; peat soils show lowest values (organic matter binding)
physics_mechanism: Surface contamination from soil adherence contributes significantly; root uptake per se very low; washing and peeling removes most surface-adhered Pu
notes: Pu-239+240 contamination >37 kBq/m2 in ~800 km2 within 30-km zone; outside this zone Pu dietary dose essentially negligible

context: Wheat/grass; extremely variable; root uptake pathway; inhalation >> ingestion pathway
physics_mechanism: Am3+ chemistry similar to rare earth elements; forms stable soil colloids like Pu4+; very low solubility; comparable or slightly lower transfer than Pu-239
notes: Am-241 is growing isotope in CEZ soils (ingrowth from Pu-241); alpha emitter (5.49 MeV); primary exposure is inhalation not dietary; 59.5 keV gamma enables aerial survey detection
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; Am-241 Belarus PMID:15196842

context: Higher transfer in radishes and carrot due to root feeding zone and high soil-contact surface area
physics_mechanism: Higher Fv for Am in root vegetables vs cereals; surface contamination dominates; dietary dose still negligible relative to inhalation
notes: In CEZ areas with >37 kBq/m2 Am-241 (which is still increasing): agricultural use restricted; am241_ingrowth_timeseries_REAL.csv
source: OSTI Am-241 soil-plant; IAEA TRS 472 2010

context: Time-dependent decrease in soil-to-plant transfer factor; 1986 values 10-50x higher than 2010 values for same soil activity
physics_mechanism: Clay mineral fixation of Cs-137 (illite vermiculite): Cs+ enters interlayer sites of clay minerals ('frayed edge sites'); becomes non-exchangeable over years to decades; reduction in exchangeable fraction → lower plant uptake
notes: This aging explains why CEZ is still contaminated but food crops outside CEZ are now mostly within limits despite elevated soil Cs-137; mushrooms/forest bypasses fixation mechanism
source: Radiocaesium fixation review Absalom 1995; IAEA TRS 472 2010; Nisbet and Woodman 2000 PMID:10688450

context: K fertilizer competitive exclusion of Cs+ from K+ plant uptake channels; used as countermeasure in Belarus/Ukraine
physics_mechanism: Potassium and Cs compete for the same plant uptake transporters; adding K fertilizer (at 200-400 kg/ha) reduces Cs-137 crop uptake by 33-50%; primary agricultural countermeasure
notes: More effective in K-poor soils; 2-14x reduction in contaminated products reported (decontamination_countermeasures_REAL.csv); not effective for Sr-90
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; Chernobyl Forum environment 2005; Nisbet and Woodman 2000

context: Liming raises pH and adds Ca2+ which competitively reduces Sr2+ uptake; primary Sr-90 countermeasure
physics_mechanism: Ca2+ and Sr2+ use same uptake transporters; high soil Ca reduces Sr-90 fractional transfer to plants; also reduces I-131 (minor); does NOT reduce Cs-137 uptake
notes: 10-30x reduction in Cs-137 in podzolic soils from liming (primarily via pH effect on clay fixation); lime was applied to 2 million ha in USSR post-Chernobyl
source: IAEA TRS 472 2010; Chernobyl Forum environment 2005; decontamination_countermeasures_REAL.csv
